instructions: Finely dice half the yellow onion, mince the garlic and thinly slice 3 of the green onions.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the pork, the salt and the pepper.
Break the pork up with a spatula and cook for 5 minutes, until it's browned and there's no pink left. Leave it alone for the first minute so it browns.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, until it's soft. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the coleslaw mix, the soy sauce, the sesame oil and the sugar. Stir well and cook for 5 minutes, until the coleslaw mix is wilted and tender.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide it into 4 containers. It keeps in the fridge for 3 days and is good cold or reheated in a skillet or the microwave until hot.
method_notes: Natasha's Kitchen (4.97, 407 ratings) is the lead, though it uses beef. Once Upon a Chef (4.89, 131 ratings) uses ground pork, which is what this one uses, with Natasha's browning order and sauce. Natasha adds carrot and sliced cabbage, Once Upon a Chef uses a bag of coleslaw mix and ginger and scallions, and this one takes the coleslaw mix so the effort stays small. Once Upon a Chef tops it with sweet and sour sauce and cashews, which this version leaves out. It follows Natasha's 3 day fridge time.
